Originating on the remote Fair Isle, part of the Shetland Islands, about 100 miles off the northeastern coast of Scotland, this beautiful, intricate, and colorful folk knit style has a rich history dating back centuries. Our timeless and cozily-elegant collection of socks and sweaters honors that rich history.

“Leno cloth” refers to a mesh-like weave known as karami-ori. Its subtly textured surface creates depth even in solid colors, allowing a single shirt to stand out with understated elegance. Woven using specialized looms, this fabric is relatively rare in the market and carries a distinctive presence as a summer shirting material.
Thanks to its open weave structure, it offers excellent breathability and keeps the fabric off the skin, ensuring a cool and comfortable feel even in humid conditions. The pronounced texture also enhances both visual freshness and a sense of refinement. Compared to the similar model “FQNS16,” this version features a finer mesh structure, making it easier to pair with wool suits and jackets. For those who wear ties in summer, its refined texture also broadens the range of suitable tie options.
Design
The collar adopts the “FRANCESE” style, balancing a sharp look when worn with a tie and a clean, relaxed impression when the top button is undone.
The collar points are designed to naturally follow the collarbone, maintaining a stable, elegant shape without lifting.
